solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tailored suit in a foreign land

indicators.note: a tailored garment has been cut and reshaped, so the letters are refashioned into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A made-to-measure suit bought somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African country, so it is a land foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: Pasta to order in one round container, finally

indicators.note: the preceding string of words goes round, enclosing, the letter that follows
finally points to the closing letter of the preceding word, the only one used

blocks.note: taken as written
to tell someone to do something is to order them
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
the final letter of the word container

explanation.surface: A diner orders pasta served in a round dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to order' looks like a phrase meaning made to request, but 'to' and 'order' are separate pieces; the R is enclosed just after the opening pair of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortellini are small ring-shaped stuffed pasta parcels, a kind of pasta.

clue.text: Audible denials from 15 figures

indicators.note: audible means heard, so we want a word that is spoken the same as the denials

blocks.note: nein is German for no, the denial you would hear from someone in Vienna (15 across)

explanation.surface: People in Vienna keep saying no within earshot of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 across is VIENNA, so the denials are in German: nein, which is said like the number nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nines are numerals, and figure is another word for a written number.

clue.text: Something pressing? Sadly, it means nothing — about right

indicators.note: things that turn out sadly have gone wrong, so the letters are put out of order
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter O looks like zero, nothing
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that a pressing matter turns out to mean nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something pressing' suggests an urgent matter; the question mark hints at pressing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam iron is used to press creases out of clothes, so it is literally a thing that presses.

clue.text: Improves as noon strikes?

blocks.note: the morning, a.m., is the stretch of day that noon closes
when noon strikes, the morning finishes

explanation.surface: Something gets better just as the clock strikes twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a whole: when noon strikes, a.m. ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text or law is to correct it, making it better.

clue.text: Polish Yankee's gem

blocks.note: to polish something is to rub it
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A jewel belonging to an American, perhaps from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P tempts you to read Polish as the nationality; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a red precious stone, a kind of gem.

clue.text: Heads for ravine in awfully narrow coastal inlet

indicators.note: the heads of words are their leading letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for a gorge that sits within a very narrow inlet of the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a drowned river valley forming a long narrow sea inlet, as on the Spanish coast.

clue.text: European ale in GB getting drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A continental visitor gets drunk on beer in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian is a person from Belgium, a country in Europe.

clue.text: Manage to flee

blocks.note: first meaning: to be in charge of, as with a business
second meaning: to escape at speed

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in getting away.
explanation.definitionFit: Run covers both operating a business and hurrying off away from danger.

clue.text: Stares at yours truly and cries out loud

indicators.note: out loud means spoken, so we want words that are heard like these

blocks.note: yours truly is the speaker, I, which is said like eye
to bawl is to cry loudly

explanation.surface: Someone glares and then bursts into noisy tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is an informal idiom for staring hard at them.

clue.text: Surreal yet real, Vic, in an imaginative way

indicators.note: something surreal is dreamlike and distorted, so the letters are distorted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend named Vic that an artwork is surreal yet real, an imaginative piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To act creatively is to use originality and invention, which is behaving imaginatively.

clue.text: Regular features of exposé on ME racecourse

indicators.note: features at regular intervals are every other letter, starting from the first

blocks.note: letters one, three, five, seven and nine

explanation.surface: A tabloid exposé about me shows up regularly in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom, in Surrey, is the English racecourse that hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a famous horse-racing course, home of the Derby.

clue.text: Tramp around island to find collection of papers

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word's letters enclose the second

blocks.note: a dosser is British slang for a vagrant who sleeps rough
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A down-and-out searches an island for a lost file.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of documents gathered on one person or subject.

clue.text: Family time in view: hugging one!

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first pieces go within the word for view

blocks.note: kin are relatives
T is the abbreviation for time
a sight is a view

explanation.surface: Family time spent in plain view, everyone embracing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is figure-hugging: 'one' stands for the body the garment clings to.
explanation.definitionFit: Skintight clothing fits so closely that it clings to the wearer's body.

clue.text: Learning about a hotel in Pakistani city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for learning wraps the letters that follow

blocks.note: lore is traditional knowledge or learning
taken as written
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Studying a hotel located in a city in Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is the capital of Punjab province and a major city in Pakistan.

clue.text: One interrupting Speaker — drat! — Liberal, before short hesitation

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the final letter of the word for hesitation is lopped off

blocks.note: both are mild exclamations of annoyance
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
erm is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A Liberal shouts 'Drat!' at the Speaker of the House, then hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes Speaker look like the Commons chair; it is anyone making a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A heckler is someone in an audience who shouts interruptions at a public speaker.

clue.text: Bargain ultimately not available after struggle to produce capital

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
the final letter of bargain
n/a is the usual abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: Shoppers fight over a bargain that has sold out, a scramble for capital.
explanation.walkthrough: N/A on a price list means not available; 'capital' looks like money but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Coppers in change initially pocketed by Rod

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of these words are kept
something pocketed is put inside, so these letters sit within the word for rod

blocks.note: a pole is a long rod
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Pennies in someone's loose change are slipped into a pocket by a man called Rod.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers looks like small change; it is British slang for police officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppers is British slang for police officers, so collectively the police.

clue.text: Thumbs down shattered Donna & co

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are smashed and reassembled

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, ignoring the ampersand

explanation.surface: An exhausted Donna and her friends give something the thumbs down.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is a colloquial refusal, the spoken equivalent of a thumbs-down gesture.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval, note, for the whole orchestra?

blocks.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A conductor tuts at a wrong note played by the full orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is a musical direction meaning all performers play together.

clue.text: Opera, not from southern California

blocks.note: to is the opposite of from
S is the abbreviation for southern
CA is the postal code for California

explanation.surface: An opera company that does not come from southern California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not from' reads as a deletion signal; it is simply the opposite of from.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's well-known opera, first performed in 1900.

clue.text: Having rest of peelings thrown out?

indicators.note: letters thrown out are scattered, landing in a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has the rest of the vegetable scraps thrown in the bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest of' looks like 'remainder of'; rest belongs with Having and means repose.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping is taking one's rest, so someone asleep is having a rest.

clue.text: Some waiter arrives in time

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so the letters are a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A waiter turns up in time to serve.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, a stretch of time.

clue.text: Girl from eastern America coming west

indicators.note: in an across answer, travelling west means right to left, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
US is America

explanation.surface: A girl from the US East Coast moves out west.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a girl's name, short for Susan.

clue.text: Region that's part of Far East

indicators.note: part of means a piece taken from within the words that follow

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A region belonging to the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region, a portion of land or space.

clue.text: Mouth a sort of English?

blocks.note: first meaning: the tidal mouth of a river where it meets the sea
second meaning: the accent of south-east England around the Thames

explanation.walkthrough: Estuary English is a British accent from the Thames estuary area, between Cockney and standard speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A river's tidal mouth is called this, and the term also names a London-area accent of speech.
